title: Question about rpg maker xp and released the game in "episodes"?

posts.author: NaMosca
posts.body:
Hi, I want to know if the rpg maker xp supports the possibility in be updated with episodes for the player continue using the same save and just donwload the new episode?
for example: there will be a scene where the player can choose the episodes, but some of them will not be implemented yet, then after the developer implement it, the player can download and with the character save they can access the new content unlocked?
Also the steam supports these type of updates?
thank you very much

posts.author: Dusk_Funa
posts.body:
I do not believe it is possible to have choices carry over in an episodic RPG Maker title, unless you create a separate save file that takes every choice in your game into consideration. You would likely simply need to finish the entire game instead.
Though this title was for VX Ace, I remember an episodic one where the developer found a way around this, but it overwrote all of the player's own story inputs such as who they chose to interact with most (it had an affection system).
If that sounds like a compromise you can make, on each new episode you need only simply provide, alongside the game's download, a save file that has been completed up to the point of the new chapter's beginning.
OTHERWISE, another solution possible though bothersome is this: If your game does not possess recurring locales whatsoever, when you provide a download to the new episode, tell players to insert only the new maps' files into their already existing data folder, alongside any other resources those maps use such as tilesets or new common events. Though keep in mind I have not tested this.
Edit: I do not know how Steam works, so I can't say for how well it supports such a thing. Sorry

posts.author: Another Fen
posts.body:
If your plan is to "extend" the existing game, your old save files should generally work with some caveats.
You should not delete any existing database entries or maps that those save files may still use, but you can add new ones.
If you plan to increase the level cap or change the exp curves, you may need a fix to update the outdated exp tables.
Some scripts may not work with save states that were created without the script present, although those incompatibilities can usually be fixed.
By default, if the game detects a version mismatch, it will reload the map the player is currently on, returning all events to their original locations and canceling ongoing parallel processes.
If you make changes to a map, make sure that the player is not suddenly stuck in an obstacle after loading (If you allow saving everywhere).
